sections.heading: Storage Requirements and Cost of Ownership

claims.text: To search 10M vectors at sub-10ms speed, you may need 64GB+ of dedicated RAM.

If you cannot afford the RAM for the Fastest vector database performance, you must switch to IVF-PQ indexing, which is 5x slower but uses 80% less memory by compressing vectors into smaller subspaces.
Quantization reduces memory costs with minimal recall impact, reducing 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers cuts memory 75% while maintaining high accuracy.
For applications retrieving large result sets (k > 10,000), batch retrieval efficiency varies significantly between databases and becomes a critical factor.

# Practical Trade-offs Between Vector Databases and Traditional Search Engines for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

**Question:** What are the practical trade-offs between vector databases and traditional search engines for retrieval-augmented generation?

## Summary

Latency p99 (99th percentile) matters more than median for user experience, as slow tail queries degrade user experience more than good medians improve it. [S5] Concurrent throughput (QPS) shows behavior under actual load, with systems handling 100 simultaneous queries at 30ms outperforming single-query benchmarks that drop to 200ms under load. [S5]

## Storage Requirements and Cost of Ownership

To search 10M vectors at sub-10ms speed, you may need 64GB+ of dedicated RAM. [S2]

If you cannot afford the RAM for the Fastest vector database performance, you must switch to IVF-PQ indexing, which is 5x slower but uses 80% less memory by compressing vectors into smaller subspaces. [S2]

Quantization reduces memory costs with minimal recall impact, reducing 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers cuts memory 75% while maintaining high accuracy. [S5]

## Failure Modes and Recovery Mechanisms

For applications retrieving large result sets (k > 10,000), batch retrieval efficiency varies significantly between databases and becomes a critical factor. [S5]

## Limitations

- The evidence does not specify the exact conditions under which vector databases outperform traditional search engines in accuracy or cost of ownership.
- The evidence does not provide concrete examples of failure modes for traditional search engines under high load or data corruption.
- The evidence does not quantify the impact of quantization on recall accuracy beyond the 75% memory reduction claim.
